about.title: About us
about.intro: Club Excellence Madagascar (CEM) is a non-political, non-denominational, non-profit association working for the development of Madagascar. Education is one of its priorities.
about.intro_2: The network's members are students and professionals in Madagascar or from the Malagasy diaspora, as well as anyone wishing to contribute to Madagascar's development. As volunteers, they take part, as their availability allows, in concrete projects across several fields: entrepreneurship, popularising scientific and technical knowledge, and improving the organisation and functioning of Malagasy society.
about.pillars_text: Each branch chooses its actions according to its community's needs, around five fields. Click a field to see the details.

education.title: Education and training
education.details:
Training and certification: certified training courses and skills-building activities.
Knowledge sharing: conferences, debates and popularisation of science and technology.
Access to education: distribution of school textbooks and easier access to educational resources.
Awareness of today's challenges: raising awareness of ecological and societal challenges, encouraging critical thinking about social norms, and promoting dialogue, mutual understanding and the peaceful resolution of conflicts.

enterprise.title: Business creation
enterprise.details:
Project incubation: a nursery of entrepreneurial projects, especially for students completing a Master's degree.
Support and networking: skills sharing, mentoring and connecting members to carry out shared projects.
Funding and partnerships: building relationships with investors, companies and support organisations.
Innovation and social impact: competitions and awards for innovative initiatives that contribute to economic development, environmental protection and poverty reduction.

research.title: Scientific research and innovation
research.details:
Research support: connecting researchers, students and professionals to foster new scientific and technical projects.
Sharing knowledge: disseminating research results and popularising scientific and technological advances.
Scientific cooperation: building partnerships between universities, laboratories, companies and civil society.
Innovation for development: encouraging applied research projects and innovative solutions that meet the needs of Malagasy society.

solidarity.title: Solidarity and humanitarian action
solidarity.details:
Support for vulnerable people: solidarity initiatives for people and communities facing social or economic hardship.
Volunteer mobilisation: pooling goodwill and resources to meet concrete needs.
Public-interest projects: designing and carrying out actions that improve living conditions and foster social inclusion.
Solidarity partnerships: cooperation with associations, institutions and partners in Madagascar and abroad to extend the reach of humanitarian action.

sustainability.title: Sustainable development and social transformation
sustainability.details:
Environmental protection: promoting initiatives that preserve natural resources and support the ecological transition.
Better living conditions: supporting projects that improve access to essential services and community development.
Modernisation and digital transformation: encouraging technological innovation and digital transformation for development.
Citizenship and collective engagement: raising awareness of societal issues, promoting civic responsibility and encouraging participation in community life.

about.network_title: Branches in Madagascar and in the diaspora
about.network_text: CEM relies on a network of branches: each one carries out its own actions close to the ground, in connection with the whole network.
about.partner_title: Alongside the Ministry of National Education
about.partner_text: CEM is bound to Madagascar's Ministry of National Education by partnership agreement no. 2022-003 MEN of 21 March 2022, which aims to:

partner_goals.skills: strengthen the skills of national education staff;
partner_goals.resources: make teaching resources more accessible to pupils;
partner_goals.excellence: promote a spirit of excellence among pupils and the population.

about.partner_example: CEM notably collected school textbooks in France and sent them to Madagascar, where the Ministry distributed them to 10,000 pupils. This partnership also made it possible to organise the first General Mathematics Competition in Madagascar, in 2022.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Club Excellence Madagascar (CEM) takes the protection of your personal data seriously. This page explains what data the site collects, why, who can see it, how long it is kept and how to exercise your rights, in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and Malagasy law no. 2014-038 on the protection of personal data.

sections.title: Data controller
paragraphs: Club Excellence Madagascar, a French non-profit association (loi 1901), headquartered at {{address}} (RNA: {{rna}}, SIREN: {{siren}}). For any question about your data: {{email}}.

sections.title: Data collected
items: Member account: last name, first name, email address, phone, branch, profile photo (optional) and password (stored encrypted, never readable).

Membership and fees: amounts, dates, payment method, sender number and Mobile Money transaction reference. Card numbers are never stored by the site: they are handled directly by the payment provider.
Contributions: proposed projects and messages posted in discussions.
Donations: amount and, if you provide them, name, email and phone (receipt and thanks).
Newsletter: email address, once you have confirmed your subscription.
Technical data: IP address and browser, recorded in the security log on sign-in and on administrators' actions.

sections.title: Purposes and legal bases
items: Managing your membership, fees, member badge and participation in projects and discussions: performance of your membership agreement.
Keeping the association's accounts and issuing donation receipts: legal obligation.
Protecting the site and accounts (security log, fraud prevention): the association's legitimate interest.
Sending the newsletter: your consent, which you can withdraw at any time via the unsubscribe link in every issue.
paragraphs: Your data is never sold or used for advertising.

sections.title: Who can see your data
items: Your branch administrators and the association's Super Admin, to manage memberships and payments.
Other members whose fees are paid see your name, photo and contributions in projects and discussions.
Member badge: anyone who scans your QR code sees your name, email and branch, as long as your membership is valid. You choose whom you show it to.

Our technical providers, only to run the site: hosting (Render, servers in Frankfurt, European Union), email delivery, card payment, and automatic English translation of published content (Anthropic, United States).

sections.title: Retention periods
items: Member account: for as long as you are a member.
Former member (fee not renewed): 3 years after your last fee period ends, then the account is automatically anonymized.
Sign-up never approved, or declined: 1 year after sign-up, then automatic anonymization.
Fees and donations: 10 years, for accounting obligations. Once your account is deleted, they are kept without your identity.
Security log: 1 year.
Newsletter: until you unsubscribe.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You have the right to access, rectify, erase, restrict, object to and port your data. From your member area (Profile tab), you can at any time:
items: correct your name, phone and photo;
download all of your data (JSON file);

delete your account: your identity is erased immediately and permanently. Your fees remain in the association's accounts without any personal data, and your published projects and messages remain signed "Membre supprimé" (deleted member).

sections.title: Complaints
paragraphs: If you believe your rights are not respected, write to us at {{email}}, or file a complaint with the CNIL (www.cnil.fr) in France, or with the Commission Malagasy de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CMIL) in Madagascar.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: The site uses no advertising cookies and no audience measurement. It only keeps in your browser what it needs to work: your sign-in session, your language and your display theme. These require no consent and disappear when you sign out or clear the site's data.
To display pages, the site loads fonts from Google Fonts and map tiles from OpenStreetMap: your IP address is then sent to these services.

sections.title: Security
paragraphs: Encrypted connections (HTTPS), encrypted passwords, data access restricted to the relevant administrators, a log of sensitive actions and regular backups protect your data.

ACTIVE.title: Active members
ACTIVE.summary: You take part in the life of the association and its projects, and benefit from its support, notably for your own entrepreneurial projects. Open from the third year of a bachelor's degree and to working professionals.
ACTIVE.text: They take part in the life of the association and contribute to carrying out its projects. They can also benefit from its support, notably to develop their own entrepreneurial projects. Membership is open to students from the third year of a bachelor's degree, as well as to people already in professional life. This requirement reflects a fundamental ambition: to make each member not only a beneficiary of the association's actions, but also a committed actor, called upon to create value and contribute to the development of society.

BENEFACTOR.summary: You support the association's missions and projects through financial, material or any other form of contribution. Your details remain confidential.
BENEFACTOR.text: They support the association's missions and projects through financial, material or any other form of contribution. To preserve the association's independence, neutrality and secular character, people holding political office and leaders of religious groups may not become benefactor members. People who have been convicted by a court are also excluded.

page.title: Opportunities to go further
page.intro: Through its partnerships, the Club supports its members in their studies, research and projects.

italy.title: Further studies in Italy
italy.p1: Through its partnerships, the Club supports students finishing their first year of a Master's or in their second year in preparing and carrying out their plan to continue their studies in Italy.
italy.p2: This is not a scholarship scheme, but support through each stage of the journey: preparing the project, the steps required before leaving, and follow-up during the programme in Italy.
italy.p3: To benefit from this support, the student must be a member of the Club and belong to one of its branches.
italy.apply_intro: Fill in the form, together with:
italy.apply_letter: a cover letter (5 lines maximum) presenting your plans, commitments and means;
italy.apply_dossier: the financing file, which may be a project to carry out through CEM.

research.title: Research and international mobility
research.p1: Through the partnership between Club Excellence Madagascar, the international CEDIMES network and the EGSS Faculty, students finishing their second year of a Master's can access calls for projects and mobility opportunities for researchers offered by CEDIMES.
research.p2: Some CEDIMES services and schemes are reserved for its members. To take full advantage of the opportunities offered, you therefore need to join the network directly.
research.p3: To learn more about the membership conditions and the opportunities offered, visit the CEDIMES website.

innovation.title: Innovative projects and social impact
innovation.p1: Club Excellence Madagascar encourages its members to design and carry out innovative, viable projects with a strong social impact. It provides support, training, networking and partnership-seeking schemes to help project leaders turn their ideas into concrete achievements. The Club is not a funding body and does not guarantee any allocation of funds.
innovation.p2: True to its motto “Excel to serve”, the Club aims to train people able to create value and contribute to the development of their society. The support offered rests on one conviction: solid projects are built through work, rigour, initiative and perseverance, not through the search for funding alone.
innovation.p3: The Club thus wishes to encourage a culture of responsibility and commitment: training pioneers who take initiative and bring solutions, rather than passive beneficiaries waiting for aid.
